subject: Numbers
title: Meet Number 1 (Ages 2-4)
description: Learn what the number 1 means and where you see it.
lessonContent: The number 1 tells how many things you have. Look around your room and find 1 objects you can touch. Count them slowly: one, two, up to 1. When you see the digit 1, remember that picture in your mind.

funFact: Athletes often wear jersey number 1 when it is their favorite digit.
amyExplanation: Numbers are labels for amounts. 1 means a set of 1 things, not a random squiggle.
audioText: Let's explore the number 1. Can you find 1 things near you?

subject: Counting
title: Count From 1 to 5 (Ages 2-4)
description: Practice counting forward in order without skipping.
lessonContent: Counting forward means saying numbers in order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Point to each object as you say one number. If you skip a number, the total will be wrong, so go slowly and match one touch to one word.
questions: What number comes right after 1?
How many numbers are from 1 to 5?
Say the list out loud: 1 to 5.
funFact: Bees can share directions by dancing in patterns—nature uses counting too.
amyExplanation: Each step up adds one more. Your voice and your finger should move together.
audioText: Count with me from 1 to 5. Tap each item as you say the number.

subject: Addition
title: Adding Small Groups 1 (Ages 2-4)
description: Combine two groups to find the total.
lessonContent: Addition puts groups together. Add 1 and 1 together. Picture 1 + 1 as blocks in two piles, then push the piles into one line and count every block.

description: Find what is left after some are removed.
lessonContent: Subtraction tells what remains. Start with 1, take away 1. Draw the starting amount, cross out the part that leaves, and count what is still there.
questions: Does subtraction make the number bigger or smaller?

description: Split a total into equal shares.
lessonContent: Division shares fairly. Split 1 into groups of 1. Deal one to each friend, then another round, until nothing is left. The rounds tell the answer.
questions: If 12 cookies go to 4 friends, each gets?

amyExplanation: Divide asks "how many each?" Everyone gets the same when it is fair.

subject: Reading
title: Read and Understand 1 (Ages 10-12)
description: Read a short passage and answer meaning questions.
lessonContent: Read aloud: "On Africa, students read books that teach stories and facts. A dog appeared in a tale about teamwork." Point to each word. After reading, retell the sentence in your own words without looking.
questions: Who or what is the story about?
Which word tells the color or place?
Retell one sentence in your words.
funFact: Reading aloud helps your eyes and ears learn together.
amyExplanation: Read once for sounds, once for meaning.
